chapters.title: Products
chapters.subtitle: What you sell, with its price

steps.text: Products are what your store sells. This video shows why a product's price lives with its content, how products, currencies and listing pages fit together, and how to use every product screen.

chapters.title: Why products
chapters.subtitle: One place for what you sell

steps.text: Every store starts with the same question: what do we sell, and for how much? Prices, pictures and descriptions kept in spreadsheets and scattered pages go out of date quickly.
Goods, services and digital items each need a price. Some things you only list, such as homes or cars, and they need a price or an inquiry button, but no cart.
The Products module keeps the price with the content. A product is an ordinary page of your site, with a price, pictures, and rules for how it sells.
Shoppers get a shop page with filters and sorting, and the cart, the checkout and the orders all read the same price.
A product is a content item whose type has the Product part. The part holds the price, the currency, a compare-at price, a sale price and a SKU.
Commerce, Products lists every product. Commerce, Product Listings holds the pages that show products to shoppers, with filters and sorting.
Commerce, Currencies holds the currencies you sell in. Extra features add variants, bundles, grouped products, comparison, recommendations, product feeds and search indexes.
Which products can be bought online, and how a price is shown, is decided on the content type. A single product can override it.
Open Commerce, Currencies. These are the currencies every product price can use, so add only the ones you sell in.
Click Add Currency. Enter the Currency code, which is three letters such as CAD, and a Display name such as Canadian Dollar.
Click Save. The new currency is listed with Edit and Delete. Its code cannot change, but you can rename it, and every product editor now offers it.
Open Commerce, Products. Every product is listed here with its status. Use Search to find one, and Edit to change it.
Click New Product. The Content tab holds everything about the product. Enter a Title. Leave the Permalink empty, and it is made from the title when you save.
Enter the Price and choose its currency. Leave Use the default currency to use the one set on the content type.
Compare-at price is the old price: when it is higher, the shop shows it struck through with the saving. Enter a SKU, and tick Featured to show the product first.
Under Images, click Add media, open the products folder in the media library, tick a picture and click OK. Then write the Description, and enter the Weight, which weight-based shipping rates use.
Click Publish. The product is on sale as soon as it is published, and it appears in the list.
Open a product to set how it sells. A Sale price makes the product sell at that price, with the regular price struck through. Sale runs sets the dates.
Quantities and volume pricing limits how many a buyer can add: At least, At most, and In packs of. Volume discounts give a percentage off each from a quantity.
Role discounts give signed-in roles, such as wholesale buyers, a percentage off. A buyer gets the best of their role and volume discounts, not both.
Under Personalization, Add-ons are the extras a buyer chooses on the product page, such as gift wrap or an engraving, each with a Label, an Extra price, and what it is Charged on.
Sold elsewhere is for a product you only promote. Enter its address, and its card links there instead of showing Add to cart.
Click Publish, then open the product on the shop. The page shows the sale price and the volume discount, and the gift wrap add-on is offered, and the cart works the final price out for you.

chapters.title: Product types and sales modes
chapters.subtitle: Set once on the content type

steps.text: How products sell is set once on the content type. Open Content, Content Definition, Content Types, and edit Product.
Click Edit next to the Product part. Product Type says whether it is a Good, a Service or Digital. Default currency is used by products that do not choose one.
Sales mode decides whether products are Purchasable, Listing only, or chosen Per item. A listing only product is shown and filtered, but never added to a cart.
Price display shows the price, shows a label such as Call for price, or hides it. An Inquiry button and an Inquiry link send interested visitors somewhere else.
Add Parts offers Product prices, for several ways to buy one product, such as monthly and yearly, and Product variants, for sizes and colors.
Open Commerce, Product Listings. The Shop page is a listing: an ordinary page that shows products. Edit it to change what shoppers can do.
Products chooses every product type, or only some. Under Filters, Choose filters lets you pick the filters, and drag them into order.
Sorting sets the sorts shoppers can choose, and the Default sort. Paging offers numbered pages, a Load more button, or Infinite scroll.
Layout sets a grid or a list, the Image shape and the page sizes. Keyword search adds a search box, and a Search index can replace the database search.
On the shop, shoppers filter by Featured or Price, sort, and switch between the grid and the list. Every combination has its own web address.
Product Comparison adds a Compare tick box to every card. Shoppers tick up to four products, such as these three, and a bar at the bottom of the page counts the products they picked.
Compare opens a page that sets the products side by side: their prices, their stock, and a row for each specification.
Open a product to see the other features. Products in this group puts several products on one page, such as the pieces of a set.
Upsells are better or bigger choices shown as You may also like, and Cross-sells go with the product and appear in the cart.
Under Bundle, Made of lists the products in a kit, sold at the bundle's own price, with stock worked out from its parts.

chapters.title: Product feeds and search
chapters.subtitle: Reach other channels, search a large catalog

steps.text: Open Settings, Commerce, Product feeds. It publishes your catalog to Google Merchant Center, Meta and TikTok, and as a spreadsheet, and it lists the feed addresses.
The page says how many products the feed holds, and warns about any it would refuse, such as a product without a photo. You can set a Brand, a Condition, and a Feed key to keep the feed private.

For a large catalog, turn on Product Search with Lucene, Elasticsearch or Azure AI Search under Configuration, Features. A listing does not use it yet: you also create the index under Search, Indexes, and choose that index on the listing. Then the listing ranks keyword matches with it.
A shop: goods with pictures, SKUs and sale prices, shown on a listing with filters and sorting, and bought through the cart.
Listings without a cart: homes or cars set to Listing only, with a hidden price or Call for price, and an inquiry button.
Wholesale: a minimum quantity, packs, volume discounts, and a role discount for your trade customers.
Gifts and kits: add-ons for engraving or wrapping, bundles for starter kits, and upsells and cross-sells to raise the order.
Keep the price with the content, choose how each product sells, and let the shop page do the rest. Thanks for watching.
